name: Tsum
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Liu, Naijing. 2023. Segmental and prosodic phonology and morphophonology in Tsum, a language of Nepal. PhD thesis, Australian National University. 298 pp. ANU Open Research handle 1885/307369.
catalog_locator: Abstract (unnumbered front matter, p. 7); Section 2.4 'Tone', p. 64; Section 2.4.3.1 'Domain of tonal assignment', p. 71; Table 2.26 discussion, p. 72; Section 2.5.2 'Phonological word (PW)', pp. 83-84; Section 2.2.3.1 'Vowel length', p. 43; Conclusion chapter, p. 229.
catalog_quote: Tsum is a word tone language with five contrastive tones. [Abstract] ... Tsum is a tonal language. This section discusses tone in Tsum from a phonological viewpoint. [p. 64] ... Tsum is not a typical word tone language as in some other Tibeto-Burman languages, nor a syllable tone language, as in Sinitic languages (Liu, 2015). Based on the available data, I argue that the domain of tone in Tsum should be the phonological word instead of syllable. [p. 71] ... Table 2.26 clearly illustrates that the tone of the compound words is determined by the underlying tone of the first syllable and realised as its corresponding tone on disyllable in the compounding form. [p. 72] ... In Tsum, the smallest prosodic unit is a syllable. By saying word tone, 'word' refers to the phonological word and it in most cases correlates with the lexical word. [p. 83] ... The phonological word (also known as the prosodic word) is the basic unit of Tsum intonation and the tone-bearing unit. A lexical word usually consists of one phonological word with one or more syllables and is assigned one of the lexical tones as shown in the first three lines in Table 2.33. Multi-word expression consists of more than one phonological word as indicated by the tone. [p. 84] ... In terms of prosody, Tsum is a word tone language, and it has five tones: H, M, L, LH, and HL. [p. 229]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: No word-stress rule is given: the only prosodic description of Tsum is tonal. Five contrastive word tones (H, HL, M, L, LH) are assigned at the level of the phonological word; in disyllabic words the surface melody (e.g. H.HL, L.HL) is fixed by the underlying tone of the first syllable rather than by per-syllable tones (Table 2.26, pp. 71-72). The thesis never mentions stress, accent or prominence at word level.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonal exceptions concern tonal vs non-tonal nominal suffixes and grammatical tone on verbs (Ch. 3-4).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (usually = lexical word, including stem+suffix); citation forms and compounds discussed for tone only. Intonation (Ch. 5) is described in AM terms with focus marked by an H* pitch accent, but this is phrase-level, not lexical stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Liu 2023 describes the Tsum of Tsum Valley (Chhekampar/Chumchet, Gorkha District, Nepal) based on fieldwork in the valley and Kathmandu; dialect variation (upper vs lower valley) is discussed in section 1.3.3 but no separate glottocode applies. Matches tsum1240 [ttz].

sources.note: Nothing. The word 'stress' occurs once in 298 pages, in a bibliography entry (Selkirk 1980); 'accent' only in the intonation chapter's discussion of English/AM-theory pitch accents and focus. Ch. 2 describes Tsum as a tonal language (p. 64) with five contrastive word tones H, HL, M, L, LH; tonal domain = phonological word, not syllable (p. 71); disyllables take a fixed pattern (e.g. H.HL) determined by the first syllable's underlying tone (pp. 71-72, Table 2.26); phonological word is the tone-bearing unit (pp. 83-84).

sources.note: Primary audio/annotation deposit behind Liu 2023. The thesis appendix (copy, pp. 263-265) lists the archived sessions by ID, including tone-targeted elicitation such as 'ttz-20221116-TB-casetone' (case marking and tone), 'ttz-20220415-TB-pword-2-3' (phonological word), 'ttz-20220501-TB-reduplication', 'ttz-TBs-20210828-roundedV', plus Mark Donohue's 2013/2016 noun and numeral recordings (ttz-Tsum-20161214-nouns-noun+DAT). It is data supporting the five-word-tone analysis, not a tone statement in itself. DataCite records seen; PARADISEC catalog itself was behind an automated-access block today…
